findings.statement: TNFa pathway activity is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism; the PURSUIT placebo arm shows nothing (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]).

NFkB activity is higher in infliximab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]) and in several other arms including placebo, so it is a general severity axis; it is not elevated in the aminosalicylate arm of PROTECT (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]).

JAK-STAT activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but does not survive correction in golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]), so it is not a uniform anti-TNF-resistance signal.

TGFb activity is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but equally with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]), so this is severity, not a drug-specific stromal mechanism.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), yet the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]) and the placebo trend is in the same direction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]); nothing survives in golimumab, infliximab or vedolizumab, so it is a severity marker, not a drug-specific one.

TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), and the interaction is not significant; it marks severity.

CXCL8 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) and with placebo non-response in UNIFI (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]); in the adalimumab single-cell atlas it shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters, only post-treatment changes in some cell states.

CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all cohorts, clinical-stage antagonists exist), but its association with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) is mirrored in placebo (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]); neutrophil burden and severity, not a drug-specific mechanism.

Baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); the drug's own target does not stratify response.

Baseline ITGB7 is not associated with vedolizumab response (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]); no target-expression stratifier emerges for gut-homing blockade.

CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate (antibody-tractable, no clinical drug); transcripts are mostly from inflammatory fibroblasts, only a minority of the signal is retained after composition correction (retained [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2764]) and vital-organ RNA reaches [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM, the highest of the group; functional and genetic evidence is missing.

CPXM1 is a stromal (fibroblast) candidate replicated in a second single-cell dataset, with retained share [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.4136] after composition adjustment, i.e. partly a fibroblast-expansion signal; low vital-organ expression but no genetics or mechanism evidence.

LAX1 is made mainly by plasma and T cells and the lineage is not replicated in the second dataset; only a small share survives composition correction (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]), so it likely reflects immune infiltration rather than a tissue change, despite very low vital-organ expression.

XKR9 is the only top novel candidate classed as intrinsic (epithelial; retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]), but it is up in only a subset of cohorts and only a small fraction of cells express it, so replication is weaker.

caveats: Response cohorts are small outside UNIFI; null results in golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab and ACT1 reflect low power.
All associations are baseline and observational; the placebo comparison separates severity from drug mechanism only partly, and PURSUIT placebo is tiny.
Adalimumab single-cell cohort has few patients (leads, not predictors); OSM shows no significant cell-state difference there.
Most novel candidates are partly composition-driven and lack genetic or functional evidence.
